newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican delegation goes to Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Vatican delegation goes to Vietnam.

text.p: The Vatican said on Monday that it had sent a high-level delegation to Vietnam to discuss Church problems with government officials.
"The delegation will meet government authorities to deal with problems regarding the Catholic Church in that country," the Vatican said in its daily bulletin.
It said the delegation, which left Rome on Sunday, was led by Cardinal Claudio Maria Celli, a senior Vatican official and expert on China and Vietnam.

He was accompanied by Monsignor Celestino Migliore, the Vatican undersecretary for relations with states, and Monsignor Barnabe Nguyen Van Phuong, an official of the Congregation for the Evangelisation of Peoples, the Vatican said.
Relations between Vietnam's communist government and the Holy See have improved in recent years along with a general easing of controls on religious freedoms.
But Hanoi has insisted on the right to veto decisions on church appointments and has turned down several Vatican nominations for bishops' posts.
Vietnam has a Catholic community of some seven million people, second largest in east Asia after the Philippines. Most of the country's 75 million population are Buddhist.
The official Vietnam News Agency said on Saturday that the delegation would stay for five days.
